column4: Description
Run TinyAya-Earth on Ollama with 5-10 tool defs in EN/SW/LG. Measure JSON validity and F1. This is the kill-or-continue gate.
column13: JULIA: Share zero-shot results immediately. Go/no-go on the whole approach. We tested the models on 33 tests and we got interesting initial results but the evaluation is too small to make a conclusion.

column4: Use Command A to generate ~600 tool-calling examples (200 EN, 200 SW, 200 LG) across 5-10 tool schemas. Native speaker validation in parallel.
column13: Start EN+SW on D1, LG on D2. Sa'ad/oj can help validate Swahili examples.

column4: Systematic: system prompts with tool schema injection, few-shot examples, constrained decoding via llama.cpp grammars. Measure F1 at each stage.
column13: JULIA: Compare zero-shot vs prompted. Discuss if constrained decoding is enough alone.

column4: Fine-tune TinyAya-Earth on synthetic dataset using Unsloth (QLoRA, 4-bit). Colab T4 or RunPod A100. Multiple runs: LR sweep, data mix, epochs. Select best checkpoint.
column13: JULIA D4: Share run 1 training curves. D5: Compare runs. D6: Final model selection rationale.

column4: Convert best checkpoint to GGUF (Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M). Create Ollama Modelfile with tool-calling prompt template. Verify inference.
column13: Can start with run 1 checkpoint while Bronson continues sweeps.

column4: Automated eval pipeline: load test set, run inference, compute F1 / schema compliance / intent routing accuracy. JSON + markdown output.

column4: Catch-up on anything that slipped. Document decisions, update experiment log. Prepare for Week 2 integration.
column13: JULIA: Week 1 retrospective. Share results summary. Plan Week 2 priorities together.

column4: Core service: load GGUF via llama.cpp NDK, expose AIDL interface. Client sends text in any language, Facade understands, generates tool call, executes, returns result.
column13: JULIA D8: Architecture review. D9: First on-device inference demo. D10: Execution layer working.
